summary: Episodes 29-56 are the Fuun Ryuko Hen block's second half and they adapt the manga in almost unbroken running order: the Fang Clan finale and Jagi (ch 36-44), Amiba's Village of Miracles (45-51), Cassandra (52-61), Raoh's first appearance and the Ken/Toki vs Raoh duel (61-72), Medicine City and Yuda (73-82). All 25 anchorable rows land between the fence anchors, strictly ascending 38 -> 82, at an even ~1.9 chapters per episode; only the Cassandra escape (eps 42-43) and the Rei/Yuda finale (55-56) need page-level care. Three sources carry the block: hokuto.fandom's chapter pages + character `appearances` reverse index (the wave-3 trap is right — there are no episode pages, but there ARE 245 chapter pages and a per-episode Filler page), RQ87's per-episode 'Manga differences' site, and hokutosite.sakura.ne.jp's Japanese per-episode 漫画版との違い. The fence's upper end is WRONG: ep 57 is a clip show whose only manga content is Rei's death, the last pages of ch 82 (Rei = ch 26-82; ch 83 opens the Souther arc and is animated in ep 59) — repair 83 -> 82. Two typing findings: ep 53 is an anime-original Blue Town/Nova plot quoting one manga scene (Yuda killing Dagar, ch 78) — filler + graft under T28, so it takes no anchor (A1); ep 54 is half the manga's Shinreidai sequence and half an anime-original raid — mixed. Eps 38 and 41 stay filler and take graft annotations for the fragments they quote.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 36 (cont.; includes the Gojiba fight, which the manga plays BEFORE ep 28's Ken/Rei duel) - 38
anchors.note: Fang King's death is ch 37 ('Time Limit of Death' = Ken's 5-second countdown, verbatim in the JP synopsis); the village aftermath, Airi's sight restored, 'he only ever wore a helmet' and Jagi's debut are ch 38 ('Evil Glare!' = the masked man's eyes). Jagi's fandom index is Manga ch. 38-44 / Anime ep. 29-32. First-time ch 36 pages open the row (A10 'pages, not numbers'): both comparison sites state the Gojiba fight sits in the manga between the knife-throwing and the forced duel — ep 28 skipped it, ep 29 plays it.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 39 (+ ch 41's Ken/Jagi sparring flashback lifted forward — see the graft annotation)
anchors.note: Ch 39 'Journey to a Deadly Battle!' = Ken leaving Mamiya's village (Yuria's image in his heart — Yuria is in ch 39's cast), the statue/saw village, and Jagi learning Ken is coming. A4: the END is the furthest chapter in RUNNING order, so the lifted ch-41 flashback is a graft, not the END (the ep-102/ch-129 precedent). hokutosite: 'ケンがジャギとの組手を思い出すのは原作ではマコと対峙しているときだが、アニメではジャギ部下と戦う前'.

Aki and Mako are Manga ch. 40-41 / Anime ep. 31 on both their fandom pages; ch 41 'Shifu's Prophecy!' carries Ryuken's warning (its cast is Ken, Aki, Mako, Ryuken, Jagi) and ends with Ken walking into Jagi's fortress — exactly ep 31's last beat. RQ87: the manga does not show the fight with Jagi's men, 'they both die as Kenshiro walks in and sees Jagi'.

Ch 42 'Ruthless Law' carries the succession flashback (its cast lists Raoh and Toki — the fandom's Raoh page: 'Ch 42 in flashbacks'); ch 43-44 are the Shin/Yuria revelation and Jagi's death; ch 44's title 怒拳4連弾 IS ep 32's title. Jagi's index ends at ch 44 / ep 32. RQ87: 'This episode pretty much follows the manga identically.'

One chapter only: Haystack, Gertz and Ellery are all Manga ch. 45 / Anime ep. 33, and Amiba's index opens at ch 45 / ep 33. TRAP: ep 33's title ('A Fallen Angel Has Arrived') is ch 46's title (狂気の堕天使) — title is not content here; ch 46's boxer / Habu / Gyuki material is ep 34. The three beast-men Ken fights are anime-original (RQ87: taken from the 1983 one-shot's 'Goda').

Habu is Manga ch. 46-48 / Anime ep. 34-35; the boxer brought to 'Toki' is ch 46 and the Gyuki arm-wrestling with the hidden saws is ch 47 ('Power Game of Death'). Goum's unit at the end is anime-original (both comparison sites).

Ch 48 'Tragic Reunion!' (Habu's death — his index ends at ch 48; Yu's family) and ch 49 'Beneath a Tragic Star!' (the scar on Toki's back, Toki's evil origin, Yu's father killed). Yu dies in the manga and is saved in the anime (both sites).

Nevada is Manga ch. 50 / Anime ep. 36 (he is the tell that the imposter is Amiba); Amiba's index ends at ch 51 'The Sad Genius!' and he dies at the end of ep 36 shouting 'Ken-Oh'. Rei/Mamiya/Bat fighting Amiba's troops outside is anime-original.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 52-53 (ch 53 to the shelter flashback; its closing pages — Uighur's manga introduction — are replaced by an anime-original scene)
anchors.note: Zakoru is Manga ch. 52 / Anime ep. 37. Ch 53 'The Men Who Create Legends!' carries the nuclear-shelter flashback (Yuria is in its cast); both comparison sites say the manga tells it just before the group reaches Cassandra and that the anime moved it into ep 37 (ep 39 only re-shows it as a recap). The Uighur scene that closes ep 37 (Zakoru executed for desertion) is anime-original — hence the partial ch 53 and the continue below.

Raiga and Fuga are Manga ch. 54-58 / Anime ep. 39-43 and Mitsu is Manga ch. 55-58 / Anime ep. 39; ch 54 is 'Open the Gate of Death!' and ch 55 'Sorrowful Gamble!' is Uighur's eagle/Mitsu gambit. Ep 39 ends with the gate open and Uighur facing Ken. The bandits killed in the cold open and the guard battle are anime-original; the anime kills Mitsu, who survives in the manga (both sites).

The whole Uighur duel: ch 56 'Graves of the Saviors' (the grave dug for Ken, which RQ87 and hokutosite both discuss as this episode's manga scene) and ch 57 'Laid to Rest in an Unmarked Grave!' — Uighur explodes inside that grave at the end of ep 40. Uighur's index is Manga ch. 53-57, 59.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 58-59 (ch 59 minus the Uighur-revival pages, which ep 43 plays)
anchors.note: Zarqa and Qasim are Manga ch. 58-59 / Anime ep. 41-42; ep 42 kills them both and reaches the fake Toki. hokutosite is explicit that ch 59's 'warden gets back up' scene is NOT in this episode ('獄長が起き上がるシーンは今回は無し。次回に。') and RQ87 places it in the manga before the Zarqa fight — so ch 59 straddles eps 42/43 (C1). Sojin and the plaza battle are anime-original.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 60 (+ ch 59's Uighur revival, deferred from ep 42; + a grafted fragment of ch 61 — Raoh's answer 'the heavens' to Ryuken)
anchors.note: The episode opens on ch 60 'Hokuto Ujoken!' — Toki catching the two guards' blades and killing them with Hokuto Ujo Hagan Ken, the reunion, and the Ken-Oh = Raoh realisation. A4 keeps the END at 60: hokutosite says the Raoh/Ryuken 'I desire the heavens' line comes in the manga AFTER the tiger test (ch 61), which ep 44 animates in full — so ch 61 here is a graft, not running-order coverage (the ep-102 / ch-129 precedent). The tower's collapse, Burg, and Cassandra being destroyed are anime-original (Cassandra survives in the manga).

Ch 61 'The Lost Man of Hokuto' is the only chapter in this stretch whose cast carries Ryuken — the tiger-test flashback ep 44 plays; ch 62 'The Blue Glow of Shichosei!' is Toki explaining the death omen star to Mamiya (Yuria in its cast) and the Seeker fight — Seeker is a ch-62 cast member and RQ87/hokutosite both discuss him as this episode's manga scene. Ep 44's title 死兆星 = ch 62's title.

One chapter: ch 63 'The Little Hero!' is Lin's defiance and branding, Rei finding the wounded Bat, and Rei's arrival — its cast (Airi, Lin, Rei, Ken, Bat, Gallon, the elder) is ep 45's cast exactly. Gallon is Manga ch. 63-65 / Anime ep. 44-46. The biker squadron and the elder being clubbed are anime-original.

The bearded hag (Dekai Babaa) is Manga ch. 64 / Anime ep. 46 and Kokuoh's debut is Manga ch. 65 / Anime ep. 46; ch 65 'The Malefic One Shines!' ends with Raoh before Rei, which is ep 46's cliffhanger. Ep 46's first minutes restage ep 45's ending with new animation (re-shown pages, not counted).

Ch 66 'The Illusionary Malefic Fists!' (Raoh's touki, Rei's Danko Sousai Ken), ch 67 'A Warning from the Dead!' (Rei's arrow), ch 68 'Fate That Calls for Blood!' (Raoh's Shinkesshu; Toki and Mamiya, in ch 68's cast, are shown nearing the village — RQ87 notes they can see the village barrier at this episode's end). The ch-68 boundary is the one inference here; ch 69 is fixed to ep 48 by Ryuken's presence in its cast.

Ch 69 'A Moment of Respite!' carries Ryuken (the flashback of Raoh killing him — the only chapter here whose cast lists Ryuken) and ch 70 'Like Calm Waters' is Toki's still-water technique, the lesson Toki tells Ken to watch; ep 48 ends with Raoh pinning both their feet with the sai (end of ch 70). RQ87: 'This episode pretty much follows the manga exactly.'

Ch 71 'Free Me from the Hikobaku!' is Ken breaking Toki's pressure-point hold; ch 72 'The Never-Ending Struggle' is the Ken/Raoh draw and Raoh riding out on Kokuoh — ch 73 opens the Medicine City arc, which is ep 50. The added Raoh techniques (Fusatsu Kinkoken, the Nanto secret) are anime-original per both sites.

Dog Master Galf and Seki are Manga ch. 73-75 / Anime ep. 50-51. Ch 74's own fandom summary ends exactly where ep 50 ends: 'before Seki can execute her, Kenshiro and Rei arrive to rescue Mamiya, with Kenshiro saying I don't tell my name to a dead man, at the end of the chapter.' The warehouse scenes and the dogs let loose on Mamiya are anime-original.

One chapter: ch 75 'The Dreadful Crest!' — the dogs cornering Ken, Galf's death, the UD mark on Mamiya, and Yuda revealed among his women; Yuda's index opens at Manga ch. 75 / Anime ep. 51. Zorige (the acid man) is anime-only — his fandom page lists Anime (ep. 51) with no manga entry.

Ch 76 'Nanto Rokusei Shines!!' is Dagar's report, Yuda casting out the scarred woman (Arisa: Manga ch. 76 / Anime ep. 52), the elder's account of Mamiya's past and Rei's 'you are still a woman'; ch 77 'The Edge of Despair!!' is the fortress and Dagar broken. Dagar is Manga ch. 76-78 / Anime ep. 52-53.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 78 (Komaku's report to Yuda) - 79 (Toki's Shinreidai and Rei's white-haired revival)
anchors.note: Komaku is Manga ch. 78-81 / Anime ep. 54-56. hokutosite names exactly two manga scenes in this episode — Komaku reporting to Yuda (content changed: in the manga he reports that Mamiya can see the death star) and Rei going white-haired under the Shinreidai — and calls the rest anime-original; RQ87 agrees ('the anime adds more filler ... he remains behind in his fortress'). Ch 79 'The Final Burst of Flame!' is Rei's last day and revival. See the type correction: this row is mixed, not plain canon.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 80 (minus the Nanto-Rokuseiken betrayal pages, held back to ep 58) - 81 (to the dam breaking and the ground turning to mud)
anchors.note: Ch 80 'When Nanto Rokuseiken Falls' is Yuda entering the village, the duel opening and the Hien Ryubu jealousy flashback (Raoh and Shin appear in its cast — the betrayal pages the anime cut); ch 81 'The Waterfowl Flies No More!' is Komaku blowing the dam. Ch 81's own fandom summary runs on into Ken sealing the dam, which is ep 56 — so ch 81 straddles 55/56 (C1). Both comparison sites record the cut betrayal scene and its reuse in ep 58 with Toki speaking instead of Rei.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 81 (cont.: Ken kills Komaku and seals the dam) - 82 (to Rei entering the house; his death is ep 57)
anchors.note: Ch 81's summary covers Ken defeating Komaku at the dam and sealing it with a slab — ep 56's B-plot; ch 82 'Final Farewell!' is Yuda's death in Rei's arms and Rei's goodbyes (Yuda's index ends at ch 82). RQ87/hokutosite: in the manga Komaku is made to drink his own poison rather than fight. Ch 82 straddles 56/57 — the anime holds Rei's death for the next episode (C1).

continue_points.note: Ep 37 takes ch 53's shelter flashback but not its closing pages — Uighur's manga introduction, which the anime replaces with an original scene (Zakoru executed for desertion). Ep 39 resumes at ch 54, so resume reading INSIDE ch 53 (C1); ep 38 is filler and carries nothing.
Ch 59 straddles eps 42/43: the warden rising from his grave is left out here and played in ep 43 (hokutosite: '獄長が起き上がるシーンは今回は無し。次回に。'). Resume inside ch 59 (C1).
Ep 44 opens the ch-61 tiger test in full; ep 43 has only lifted Raoh's closing line from it ('I desire the heavens'). Resume at ch 61 (C2 parity with the next episode's START).

Ep 53 is an anime-original Blue Town/Nova plot and carries only ch 78's Dagar scenes (his madness and Yuda killing him); ep 54 resumes at ch 78. Read straight on from ch 78 — nothing between 77 and 78 is skipped.
Ch 79 straddles eps 54/55: the anime substitutes Komaku's raid for Yuda's own arrival, which closes ch 79 and opens ep 55 the next morning. Resume inside ch 79 (C1).

Ch 81 straddles eps 55/56 — ep 55 stops at the flood, ep 56 carries Ken sealing the dam and the duel's end. Also skipped on the way: ch 80's pages where Rei reveals Yuda's betrayal of the Nanto Rokuseiken; the anime does not stage them until ep 58 (C3 — read them now, they are not re-read later).
Ch 82 straddles eps 56/57: Rei enters the house at the end of ep 56 and dies in ep 57, which is the chapter's last pages. Resume inside ch 82 (C1).

annotations.note: The Gojiba fight sits in the manga BEFORE the Ken/Rei forced duel that ends ep 28; the anime holds it back and plays it here, after the ruse (hokutosite: 'ゴジバが殺されるのは、原作ではまだアイリ達が人質の時だが、アニメでは後'). The buried explosives splitting the party and Rei/Mamiya's fight through the clan are anime-original — the manga has the four of them together with the Fang King as the last man standing.

The Ken/Jagi sparring flashback and Ryuken's warning about Ken's mercy are ch 41 in the manga, told while Ken faces Mako; the anime lifts them forward into ep 30 and re-shows them as a soft-focus recap in ep 31. Not counted in ep 30's END (A4).

The Amiba arc runs in manga order with anime-original padding on every row: Lin leaving Mamiya's village and Rei/Mamiya/Bat searching for her (in the manga Lin never leaves), the three beast-men (restaged from the 1983 one-shot), Yu's family made travelling merchants, Goum's unit, and Yu surviving where the manga kills him.

Filler row, quoting two manga fragments: the Suzan Tsuhi Ken master handing over his style's scroll — in the manga this is inside Toki's flashback during the Cassandra escape, and the anime deletes it from ep 43 — and Toki's smile, which the manga places just after Uighur kills an escaping prisoner. Bella and Targel are anime-only characters (their fandom pages list Anime (ep. 38) with no manga entry). Exact chapters of the two fragments are inferred from the escape/gate scenes, not stated by a source.

Cassandra's gate and the Uighur duel follow the manga, but the anime kills Mitsu (he survives in the manga), adds the bandit cold open and a full guard battle, and moves Uighur's eagle threat to before Ken's arrival.

Filler row: a Bat-and-Lin clip show whose only manga content is the closing scene — Zarqa and Qasim's royal guard cutting down Cassandra's soldiers as they arrive, the opening of ch 58 'Footsteps of Terror!'. Zarqa and Qasim are Manga ch. 58-59 / Anime ep. 41-42.

The escape from Cassandra keeps the manga's spine (the royal guard, the fake Toki, Toki's Hokuto Ujo Hagan Ken, the Ken-Oh = Raoh revelation) inside a heavily rebuilt frame: Sojin and Burg are anime-original, Raiga and Fuga are killed by Zarqa and Qasim in the manga, and Cassandra is not destroyed in the manga at all.
Ch 59's Uighur revival ('Cassandra will return to the wasteland') is deferred one episode: the manga plays it before Ken fights Zarqa, the anime after Toki is found.
Raoh's answer to Ryuken — that he desires the heavens — closes ep 43; in the manga it belongs to the tiger-test scene of ch 61, which ep 44 animates in full.

Anime-original episode (Nova, the Buldan/Blue Town raid, the decoy Yuda) quoting one manga sequence at the end: Dagar losing his mind and killing his own men, then the real Yuda killing him with Nanto Kokakuken. hokuto.fandom's Filler page: '53 - Except when Yuda kills Dagarl at the end'; hokutosite: 'ダガールが狂って部下達を殺すシーンと、ユダに南斗紅鶴拳で殺されるシーン以外は全てアニメオリジナル'.

Half the episode is the manga's Shinreidai sequence (Toki's offer, the poison as the alternative, Rei's agony and white-haired revival) and Komaku's report to Yuda; the other half — Nova's jeep, Komaku's raid on the village, Gogyan and Shikaba, Mamiya learning of the death star from Rei instead of Yuda — is anime-original.

Ch 80's pages in which Rei reveals that Yuda betrayed the Nanto Rokuseiken (leaving with 23 branches to side with Raoh) are cut from this episode; the anime stages them in ep 58 with Toki speaking instead of Rei.

repairs.why: The stored fence anchor came from batch 6 with its own '~ch 83 (+/-1)' caveat. Ep 57 is a clip show whose single manga beat is Rei's death, and Rei's death is the end of ch 82 'Final Farewell!': (1) hokuto.fandom's Rei page indexes him as Manga ch. 26-82 / Anime ep. 23-57; (2) ch 82 is the last Yuda-arc chapter and ch 83 'Nanto in Turmoil!' opens the Souther arc — its cast is Kokuoh, Raoh, Taka, Ken, Bull, Shu, with no Rei — and Taka and Bull are both indexed Manga ch. 83 / Anime ep. 59, which is where the stored anchors already put ch 83; (3) RQ87 and hokutosite both state that in the manga Rei dies seconds after entering the house, i.e. ch 82's closing pages, and that every flashback in ep 57 is anime-original. The block blurbs that say 'chapters 26 to 83' (hokuto.fandom's episode list and AFG, which reads as a copy of it) are arc-level prose, not a per-episode claim. Volume stays 10 (ch 82 is v10: 81-89). The stored continue 83 for ep 57 remains correct.

type_corrections.note: Stored canon (AFL/AFG canon). The episode's plot is anime-original — Nova's band, the raid on Buldan/Blue Town, the rescued women, the decoy Yuda — and it quotes one manga sequence at the end (Dagar's madness and death, ch 78). Under T28 an original plot that quotes a fragment is filler with a mandatory tie annotation (graft {78}), and A1 then forbids an anchor on the row. Two independent sources beyond AFL: hokuto.fandom's Filler page lists '53 - Except when Yuda kills Dagarl at the end' and hokutosite says everything but the two Dagar scenes is anime-original; RQ87 says 'Most of this episode is filler'. This follows the series' standing ruling (T6, 2026-08-25) that fandom + accounting beat AFL on this show.

Stored canon. Source and anime-original are both substantial and story-carrying (T28): the manga side is Komaku's report to Yuda and the whole Shinreidai sequence of ch 79 (Toki's offer, the poison, Rei's agony and white-haired revival); the anime side is Nova driving them home, Komaku's raid on the village, Gogyan and Shikaba, and Mamiya learning of the death star from Rei rather than from Yuda. hokutosite states only those two scenes are from the manga; RQ87 says the anime 'adds more filler' here and that Yuda himself comes in the manga. The anchor (78-79) is unaffected — mixed rows still take anchors.

structure.notes: CHAPTER SPACE confirmed independently of the fandom: en.wikipedia's 'List of Fist of the North Star chapters' numbers the same 245 chapters with the same volume boundaries the context stores (v5 36-44, v6 45-53, v7 54-62, v8 63-71, v9 72-80, v10 81-89), hokutosite states the WSJ serialisation ran '全245話', and Coamix's own digital edition (comic-zenon.com) indexes the chapters under the same numbers and titles (e.g. '第59話 静かなる巨人！の巻'). Flag #1047 (MU latest_chapter 71 vs AniList 245) is a MangaUpdates release-record artifact, not an edition: nothing in this block uses MU's numbering. SOURCES FOUND, and worth recording for the 109-151 block: (1) hokuto.fandom has NO per-episode pages (the wave-3 trap holds — only 6 stray ones) but it DOES have 245 per-chapter pages carrying volume, page count, JP title and a cast list in order of appearance, a per-character `appearances` field of the form 'Manga (ch. 53-57, 59), Anime (ep. 37-42)' that works as a two-way index, a single 'Hokuto no Ken episodes' page with a full per-episode summary, and a 'Filler' page with per-episode exceptions ('41 - Clip show until Zarqa and Qasim show up at the end'). (2) rq87.flyingomelette.com/HNK/1/<ep>/a.html — an English per-episode site with a dedicated 'Manga differences' section on every row. (3) hokutosite.sakura.ne.jp/sakuhin/gensaku/hokuto/<NNN>.html (Shift-JIS) — a Japanese per-episode synopsis with a 漫画版との違い bullet list; it is the site the wave-3 verdict cited for ep 27. The three are independent of each other and of AFL/AFG. BLOCK ACCOUNTING: eps 29-56 adapt ch 36-82 with no chapter left unanimated between the fence anchors; 25 anchors ascend 38 -> 82 (ep 53 excluded, see type_corrections). The two stored filler rows quote fragments only. AFG's block line 'Adapted from manga 26 to 83' for eps 23-57 reads as a copy of hokuto.fandom's arc blurb (same span, same phrasing shape) — treated as one source, and superseded per-row by the ep-57 repair.

flags_for_sean: EP 58's stored anchor (ep58 -> 83 [83] {83 (partial)}, batch 17) is contradicted by three sources and is the next thing to re-derive after this block. hokutosite calls ep 58 flatly 'アニメオリジナルストーリー'; RQ87 says 'Almost all of this episode isn't in the manga. The scene where Toki talks about the South Star six holy fists and Yuda's betrayal was in the manga, but this was used earlier, and Rei talks about it rather than Toki' — i.e. its one manga sequence is the ch-80 betrayal passage the anime cut from ep 55, not ch 83; hokuto.fandom's Filler page says '58 - Mostly filler, except for the origin of the Nanto Rokusei Ken'. Ch 83 itself is animated in ep 59 (Taka and Bull: Manga ch. 83 / Anime ep. 59), which the stored ep-59 anchor already says. Likely shape: ep 58 filler-or-mixed with a rearranged {80} annotation and no ch-83 anchor. Out of this task's range, so no repair proposed.

IF ep 53 is left canon rather than retyped filler, its honest anchor is END 78 / START 78 / {78 (Dagar's madness and Yuda killing him with Nanto Kokakuken)} / vol 9, confidence high — the rest of the episode has no manga counterpart. I have not put it in anchors because A1 forbids one on the type I am proposing.

EP 43's END is a judgement call between 60 and 61. I chose 60 under A4 (running order) because the only ch-61 content is Raoh's single 'I desire the heavens' answer lifted out of the tiger test that ep 44 animates in full — the same shape as the stored ep-102 graft {129}. If you would rather count first-time pages regardless of order ('pages, not numbers'), ep 43 becomes END 61 and ep 44 becomes START 61 (cont.).

AIR-DATE aside, not repaired here (lane B territory, and ep 29 was already looked at in wave 4): hokutosite prints ep 29 = 85年5月9日 and ep 30 = 85年5月23日, i.e. one week earlier than our stored 1985-05-16 / 1985-05-30. RQ87 agrees with our stored dates and explicitly notes a two-week broadcast gap before both episodes. Two-to-one for the stored values; recording it only because it is the same 5/9-vs-5/16 dispute the ep-29 flag already carries.
